correction: migrations are append-only, never edit an existing migration

allow.patch:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: migrations/0009_new.sql
+select 1;
*** End Patch

why: The user wants to allow adding a migration and block editing one. The write schema cannot tell create from edit, so this expected rule fails its own allow example. Either the schema gains an 'existing files only' or 'Update/Delete only' mode, or this becomes a reminder.
Normalisation strips sudo as a wrapper before matching, so a rule whose program is sudo may never match. The plan should say whether wrapper programs can be rule targets.

correction: kubectl apply sirf staging context pe, prod pe kabhi nahi
why: This needs a flag-with-value match. The schema's flags are bare tokens, '--context prod' (separate value) cannot be expressed, and the current context may come from kubeconfig with no flag at all.

correction: only run the tests for the package you changed, not the whole monorepo
why: Could be a rule against 'pnpm test' at the repo root, but the schema has no cwd condition, and 'the package you changed' is not visible on the call.

correction: new React components go in src/components, not src/ui
why: A write rule on src/ui would also block legitimate edits to existing files there. The correction is about where new files go, so it may be a reminder rather than a rule.

correction: use our date helper instead of adding moment.js
why: 'npm install moment' could be stopped, but the package name is the second positional, which the schema cannot match. A rule on 'npm install' would block every install.
'Shared' is not visible on the call. A rebase rule asks before every rebase, including on private branches, which may be too broad for the user.
L4c's example derivation includes 'run'. 'npm run build' does work in most pnpm repos, but the user may still want pnpm run. Whether run belongs in the derived rule is for the plan owner to decide.
The time condition cannot be expressed. A plain push rule would ask every day.

correction: don't run the e2e suite locally, it hits the shared staging DB
why: The script name is the second positional, which the schema cannot match, so this expected rule fails its own allow example. 'playwright test' would be a cleaner target, if that is what the script runs.

correction: never curl | sh an install script
why: The danger is the pipe into a shell, not curl itself. A curl rule would block every HTTP check, and the schema has no pipe-shape pattern. This fits the L7b starter policy better.
